messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 0.9 update
parts:
Given the number of examples over all the functions, there's no way it
will take less than five minutes to run. The easiest way to improve
speed on the examples is to use small data frames, so data such as
movies and diamonds should be avoided. This indicates a couple of
things to me:

(1) For help pages, either have a couple of quick examples per
function or put them in dontrun{} blocks - I'd prefer the latter,
since one can always copy and paste to the console to see how the
features work.
(2) The constraint from CRAN emphasizes the value of the on-line help
pages, so the priority of meshing Roxygen2 with helpr should probably
be upped in the short term. When the examples can be translated to the
ggplot2 home page again, perhaps links to individual pages can be put
into the help files for CRAN instead of running examples.
(3) Given that most ggplot2 calls involve the use of several functions
at a time, one can explore detailed examples more fully on a web page
than on an example page. You can see this with the scales package: the
in-function examples are pretty sterile, but are apt for the intended
function. However, you need more detailed (and hence slower) examples
to see how those functions fit in bigger picture.

Didn't know about the CRAN requirements on time limits for examples.
Useful to know...

Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 0.9 update
parts:
With donttest, the example code still exists on the help page, but
example(fun) won't work from the R prompt nor will it be run during R
CMD CHECK - you'd have to cut and paste the code into an R session,
which AFAIC isn't necessarily a bad thing. I often want a look at a
line or small chunk of example code rather than the whole thing.

I think donttest is a good compromise solution, but as I wrote
earlier, it ups the priority of getting the examples on-line, and one
of the side benefits is that more interesting and complex examples
could be included there. I view this as an opportunity, not a loss.

Dennis
